The Command of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, on the 7th of December, is probably responding to a request, but is providing information to Mr. Krajisnik, the speaker of the Assembly, about cease-fire violations carried out by the Muslims. It's the 31st of August and up until the 1st -- the 5th of November. So could you please note: "The structure of these violations and the number of projectiles involved, artillery projectiles that fell on Serb territory"? Do you see that, General?

utterances.speaker: JOHN WILSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do see that, Mr. Karadzic. There was a war going on. Both sides were firing. I think that's acknowledged by everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But these are Serb areas of town, and in these partial reports in the media, and some official reports too, it says that there was fire at the city, and it goes without saying that it was the Serbs that were doing the firing. And look at the results. Twenty-four dead, 37 severely wounded, 25 with light wounds. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN WILSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that, but I have no idea what report you're talking about, nor media coverage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, General, the speaker of the Assembly is taking part in negotiations, and at his request the commander is informing him about cease-fire violations so that he could put this to you at the conference, all the things that the Muslims are doing, that is, and the structure is here, the structure of the violations -- of the cease-fire violations that were carried out by the Muslims. Do you see in the last paragraph, that in the area of the Jewish cemetery, a mass grave for Serbs was found?

utterances.speaker: JOHN WILSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the first time I've seen a report of that, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But, General, we discussed that. Krajisnik did not ask for this for his private collection, as it were. Mr. Krajisnik is asking for this information so that we could present it at the conference. We are presenting it at the conference. You were a participant in this conference. You have to know about this. You have to evaluate this, you have to take it into consideration; right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN WILSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking about the mass grave or about the firing of artillery shells?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes -- just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Primarily violations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has already said on a number of occasions that it was around this date or the following day that he left his position as military adviser to the conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karadzic, you have two minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a four-month period from the end of August until the 5th of November, and the general at the time was part of the conference. This was his very own activity. He was supposed to have information, and we saw what his duties were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is your question to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, if you didn't know about this, didn't you have to know about it? Was it not your duty to know this?

utterances.speaker: JOHN WILSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I've already said that I acknowledged that there was a war going on and they were -- people were firing from both sides, and I don't think anybody would dispute that. But if we're talking about the total number of rounds, just quickly adding up, there's something in the order of a thousand rounds over a five-month period, it does not seem to me to be an intensive level of activity. Your troops on some days would do that before morning tea, firing into Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, that's not right. And it's not five months, it's two months, September and October, so it's two months. And if it were all to be added up, it would be a lot more. Can this document be admitted? The general said that all sides were firing, so let's see what it was that the Muslim side was firing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: His evidence is there, and the general did not know anything about this document. We'll not admit this document. Your last question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D01285. P860, that's the number, and it's already been admitted, therefore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, in your paragraph 106, you refer to the London Conference and to my agreement that Serbs concentrate heavy weapons, et cetera, et cetera. Are you aware of my letter -- or, rather, my position presented in my letter sent to the editor of "The Guardian," I think it is?

utterances.speaker: JOHN WILSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall such a letter, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's not the document. P860 or 1D01285. The Serb position is presented on the 18th of August, I think. 1D01285, please. It's a Defence exhibit, 1D01285.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think it has been --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I've got it noted as Prosecution exhibit P00860.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's it, that's it. Can it be rotated, please? I'm not sure this has been admitted. I have the wrong number here, as if it were admitted as a P document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, since at that point in time you were working for the conference, were you not interested at all in the position of the Serb side that is coming there to negotiate and that is presenting its position here in this letter? And were you aware of that position?

utterances.speaker: JOHN WILSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of the Serb position, which changed over time while I was in Geneva. I was broadly aware of what the position was, but I'm unaware of this letter to the editor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for the record, could you give the number again, Ms. Sutherland, P number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 860. Then he was correct. No, it's a different one, so I'm not sure whether this has been previously admitted. We'll admit it in case -- no, we'll deal with it separately. Let's hear your last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know, General, that the Party of Democratic Action had asked citizens from certain areas, say specifically from Trebinje, to leave Trebinje so that in three or four months' time they could ask to get Trebinje on the basis of ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: JOHN WILSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We have that document. If we have time, 1D0151. And we also have evidence of that in Professor Koljevic's diary. The Muslims first asked me to approve that, and I refused, and then they gave secret instructions for people to move out of Trebinje so that they could accuse us. The number is D1851.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There's no --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not the document, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think there's any point --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. If he didn't know about it, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The last question, General: Is it not 3:1 in favour of the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: JOHN WILSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking about here. Here, it's 5 love in favour of the Serbs, but tonight in South Africa, against Australia, is it not going to be 3 nil against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: JOHN WILSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say, Mr. Karadzic, that it will probably be in favour of the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no re-examination of the witness. I want to just add that there was five documents over the course of the two days that the Prosecution wasn't advised of that the Defence were going to use, and we would appreciate, in future, if we could be advised of all documents that they intend using during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you for that reminder. Mr. Karadzic, would you like to tender that, the last item, which was a newspaper article as to your position?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly. I thought that the Prosecution had tendered it. But if they haven't done that, then I would like to tender it as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we know whether or not it has been admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Reid advises me that the information that we got from the Defence said that it had been admitted as a Prosecution witness -- a Prosecution exhibit, but that was incorrect. So I defer to Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I don't have it on my record as an exhibit either for the Prosecution or the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What would be your position, Ms. Sutherland, as to its admission?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just one moment, Your Honour. I want to read the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The witness didn't have an idea about its content.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In that case, Your Honour, following your guide-lines, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll not admit it. The accused will have another opportunity to tender it. General, that concludes your evidence. Thank you very much for your coming a long way to the Tribunal to give it. Now you're free to go. Thank you again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may respond to the distinguished Ms. Sutherland. Today, we sent another note saying that we have not received a very important exculpatory document in relation to Ambassador Okun. There are two sources why documents are not appearing, documents that we are going to deal with; one, late disclosure on the part of the OTP, and the second reason is that witnesses give very lengthy answers. I put one question, and they give answers to three questions, and then I have to get a document out that I had not intended to tender along with that particular witness. So those are the reasons why there are some documents that we had not sent notification for earlier on. And, of course, there's the pressure of time that the Defence is under. We don't have enough time to prepare or to present what we have to present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In any event, I would expect in the future -- expect you to do your utmost to comply with that disclosure. Due to the scheduling issue, in terms of witnesses, we don't have any witnesses for this week, and I will let you know, as soon as possible, as to the date for Mr. Mandic's testimony. That said, unless there's any matter, we'll rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll sit on Monday, 2.15, to hear evidence of KDZ-185.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 28th day of June, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.
